name: responsive-release-proof
description: Prove a changed web surface at desktop and mobile before release. Use when a website, landing page, rendered frontend, or responsive CSS changed and the task includes final QA, deployment, release, or a claim that the user-visible page is ready.
scenario: Static checks passed, but the actual 390px page was 22px wider than the viewport because a visually hidden table header and long CI rail still participated in layout.
desiredOutcome: produce browser-backed release evidence and fix responsive blockers instead of treating a passing build as proof
verification: Load the actual local or staged page; verify identity, meaningful DOM, console health, a primary interaction, desktop and 390px screenshots, and scrollWidth equal to innerWidth.
positiveTriggers: Finish this landing-page release and verify desktop and mobile before shipping
We changed the responsive CSS; do the final browser QA and fix any blockers
The site build is green. Prove the real page is ready to deploy
Check this frontend at 390px and desktop, exercise the menu, and capture release evidence
negativeTriggers: Explain how CSS media queries work
Review this responsive design proposal without running the site
Write unit tests for this backend parser
Create a visual concept for a new landing page
processSteps: Name the exact page URL, primary interaction, and user-visible ready state before testing
Run the repository's static and build checks, but do not treat them as browser evidence
Open the actual built or served page in the available browser surface and verify URL, title, meaningful DOM, missing assets, and console warnings or errors
At a normal desktop viewport, inspect the first viewport, the changed sections, and at least one primary interaction
At 390px or the requested mobile width, assert document scrollWidth equals innerWidth and inspect wrapping, clipping, overlap, navigation, and touch-sized controls
If horizontal overflow exists, project the bounding boxes of elements outside the viewport, fix the smallest root cause, reload, and repeat the identical measurement
Capture desktop and mobile screenshots plus the interaction state; report exact viewports, checks, fixes, and remaining browser or flow boundaries
doneCriteria: The actual local, staged, or released page has the expected URL, title, and meaningful rendered content
No relevant console warning, framework overlay, missing asset, clipping, overlap, or horizontal viewport overflow remains
At least one primary interaction has a directly observed state change
Desktop and 390px mobile evidence correspond to the implementation being released
The handoff names exact viewports, evidence, fixed blockers, and any untested browser or state
